title: Career roadmap · Quant Analyst
summary: Build strong foundations in probability, statistics, mathematics, programming, algorithms, financial markets, and quantitative modelling to enter quantitative research, trading, risk, and financial analytics roles.

horizons.question: What can I enter now?
horizons.output: Build probability, statistics, calculus, linear algebra, Python, SQL, algorithms and financial-market fundamentals; target Quantitative Analyst Intern / Risk Analyst Intern / Research Intern / Data Analyst roles.

horizons.question: How should I specialise?
horizons.output: Develop stochastic modelling, time-series analysis, optimisation, machine learning, derivatives and financial-data skills; target Quant Analyst / Quantitative Research Analyst / Risk Quant.

horizons.question: How should I evolve?
horizons.output: Move toward quantitative research, systematic trading, portfolio analytics, risk modelling or financial engineering.

horizons.question: How can I remain relevant?
horizons.output: Combine advanced mathematics with machine learning, alternative data, high-performance computing, AI-assisted research and model-risk expertise.

blocks.label: Timeline assumption
blocks.text: This roadmap assumes a 3-year B.Sc beginning in 2026. For a 4-year honours route, use the additional year for advanced probability, stochastic processes, optimisation, machine learning, financial modelling, research, and quantitative-finance internships.

blocks.text: 4-year honours variant

Use Year 4 for advanced probability, stochastic processes, numerical methods, optimisation, machine learning, financial derivatives and a research dissertation. A strong honours project could be “Statistical modelling of market volatility”, “Factor-based portfolio construction”, or another research topic with reproducible quantitative results.
Specialisation lanes

Keep the mathematical core strong. Quantitative finance changes quickly, but probability, statistics, optimisation, numerical methods and disciplined empirical testing remain foundational. Add ML, deep learning, alternative data and high-performance computing without replacing mathematical understanding with black-box models.

Career progression

items: B.Sc Statistics & Computer Science / Mathematics & Computing
Junior Quant Analyst / Risk Quant / Quant Developer — 1–4 years
Quant Research Lead / Portfolio or Risk Modelling Lead — 12+ years
Head of Quant Research / Quantitative Strategies — 15+ years

blocks.text: Actual progression depends heavily on the employer, market, strategy and individual performance.
PhD routes
Potential research directions include:
A PhD can be particularly valuable for quantitative research roles where deep mathematical or statistical research is required.

The strongest long-term profile will combine deep mathematics, statistical reasoning, programming, financial-market understanding and machine learning. AI will increasingly assist with research and coding, but rigorous model validation, statistical reasoning, experimental design and understanding of market behaviour will remain critical.
